prompt: Write a tiny scanner where each TokenKind constant knows how to match itself: implement matchLength per constant, then tokenize an arithmetic expression into KIND:text pieces.
explanation: Giving the enum an abstract matchLength puts each token's rule inside the constant that owns it, so the scanner itself contains no knowledge of digits or operators -- it just walks values() and takes the first non-zero match. Returning a length rather than a boolean lets the caller both decide the winner and know how far to jump, which is how real lexers are structured. The loop must advance pos by the matched length (or by 1 for a space) on every pass, otherwise it spins forever.
hints: For NUMBER and NAME, walk an `end` index forward while the character qualifies and return end - pos; guard with end < text.length() so you never read past the string.
OPERATOR and PAREN can test membership with "+-*/".indexOf(text.charAt(pos)) >= 0, returning 1 or 0.
In tokenize keep an int pos, skip spaces with pos++, then loop over TokenKind.values() and break on the first positive length; if none matched, throw the IllegalArgumentException.
